proof_checks: The modified comparison proof retains bounded ordered contact with fixed positive factors, bounded Stokes approximation, the full torsion expansion and q recurrence. Negative-power terms with zero coefficient and dimension one are handled explicitly.

Strict domination chooses epsilon before the sublevel height, uses positive volume of the nonempty strict set and keeps a positive omega^n remainder. Its individual-mass corollary is not a uniform lower-mass property. Exponential comparison keeps the direction of both measure inequalities.

The capacity-test convex combination gives the two sublevel inclusions with a half-height reserve. The backwards iteration proves positivity of each remaining height before applying comparison. The Lp density bound gives both potential control and a lower density norm; neither is used as a blanket mass assumption.

Uniform compactness uses a fixed positive capacity bound and the Lp/Chebyshev estimate for the difference set. Normalized L1 compactness supplies a subsequence; uniform convergence identifies a continuous positive-background limit.

Root-integral convergence and a Gauduchon trace bound the approximation scalars above; the lower-density norm bounds them away from zero. Dimension one uses Stokes directly. The exponential mean estimate keeps lambda fixed, uses a density-weighted probability and the conjugate exponent np/(np-1).

Bounded exponential comparison proves uniqueness and order even where densities vanish. Applying continuous exponential existence to exp(-u)f proves continuity of a bounded solution. Zero-exponent barriers give a unique scalar, but do not identify a unique cluster potential.
Classical scalar uniqueness uses an epsilon positivity reserve at an extremum; the determinant need not be positive everywhere. Interchanging the potentials closes the argument.

The Hopf specialization explicitly recalls the manifold, projection, rank-one forms, fiber action and probability measures. Its mass6 normalization yields the factor4 in the averaging inequality. Equality gives base descent and, conversely, the bounded cube identity gives the correct normalized equation.

Near-minimum mass gives subsequential uniform potentials and weak Lp densities. Reflexivity and self-adjoint Haar averaging give the stated whole-sequence differences. The oscillatory example has uniform positive coefficients, exact mass1+a^2/(2*pi^2*m^2) and nonzero L1 limit2a/pi; no strong density convergence is inferred.
